newsitem.title: USA: NAR economist says housing numbers to decline.
newsitem.headline: NAR economist says housing numbers to decline.

text.p: Existing home sales will continue to decline as the U.S. economy softens to about two percent growth, John Tuccillo, chief economist at the National Association of Realtors, said Monday.

"You will see housing numbers continue to come down" to about a 3.85 million to 3.9 million annual rate later this year, Tuccillo told a press briefing after the trade group released October existing home sales data showing a 1.5 percent fall to a 3.97 million annual rate.
Tuccillo added: "we may edge up next month, but I seriously doubt it."
He said he expects 30-year fixed-rate mortgage rates to decline by about a quarter of a percentage point through the end of the year and possibly by another quarter point early next year.
If that were to occur, there would probably be a "rash" of refinancings, Tuccillo said.
The trade group is projecting 4.09 million existing home sales during 1996 and 3.84 million in 1997.
